rooms.question: Which differences disappear when a representation gives some terms less room?
rooms.ontology: An embedding represents items by positions; distances can make distinctions available or collapse them. This artifact is an authored spatial analogy, not a measured embedding from a trained model.
rooms.action: Choose two warm-coloured word labels and follow both as you move PERSPECTIVE. Compare their separation with two grey labels.
rooms.observable: Warm labels compress into a small region while grey labels spread out and move away. Label positions and visual emphasis change together.
rooms.mechanism: Seeded positions are interpolated between two authored configurations by a connected horizontal slider. The control moves geometry rather than changing a camera or retraining an embedding.
rooms.limit: The model makes compression legible but does not establish that these exact distances occur in an actual language model. Its two preselected term groups also deserve scrutiny.
rooms.variation: Existing: stop halfway and track one distinction still visible and one becoming difficult to read. Proposed: compare these authored positions with a documented measured embedding and several different groupings.
rooms.prior_bridge: The laboratory made model parameters explicit; now ask who gets represented distinctly.
rooms.next_bridge: Applied ethics moves the same question from word positions to furniture and participation.

rooms.question: Who is made easiest to address before anybody has spoken?
rooms.ontology: An affordance makes some actions easier than others. A seating plan distributes visibility, orientation and the symbolic position of a head.
rooms.action: Walk around the paired room models. Trace a line of sight from the head chair in the long-table plan, then from one chair in the circular plan.
rooms.observable: One model singles out a head position; the other arranges chairs around a shared centre. Red and green colours already suggest an evaluation.
rooms.mechanism: The default pair builds two static room models with different furniture. Other plan values are curator configurations, not visitor toggles.
rooms.limit: A circle does not guarantee equal speech, access or authority. Colour can supply the answer before the learner has examined the arrangement.
rooms.variation: Existing: defend one useful role for the head position and identify one exclusion the circle could retain. Proposed: test sightlines and turn-taking with actual groups, including mobility and hearing needs.
rooms.prior_bridge: Bias exposed unequal space between representations; furniture makes unequal access to a conversation tangible.
rooms.next_bridge: Paraconsistent engineering next asks what to do when two legitimate requirements conflict.

rooms.question: Must one account disappear before two accounts can share a system?
rooms.ontology: Two branches preserve distinct versions; a conflict records incompatibility requiring a policy. Retaining provenance differs from silently choosing a winner.
rooms.action: Inspect the two labelled pillars and the lit junction between them. Trace each branch to the meeting point before deciding what a combined result should retain.
rooms.observable: Branch A and branch B remain visible around a pulsing conflict marker. The default junction does not resolve either version.
rooms.mechanism: Static authored pillars and a pulsing sphere diagram a merge conflict. Curator variants overlap, resolve to one branch, or fork apart; no actual merge or paraconsistent inference runs.
rooms.limit: Disagreement between records is not automatically a logical contradiction. Formal paraconsistency requires inference rules that avoid arbitrary conclusions from a contradiction; the sculpture does not implement those rules.
rooms.variation: Existing thought experiment: assign the branches two incompatible dated measurements and preserve source and time before choosing a policy. Proposed: a small rule table showing which inferences survive a contradiction.
rooms.prior_bridge: Furniture distributed participation; now two participants may contribute incompatible claims.
rooms.next_bridge: Situated computation asks what conditions gave each claim its authority.

rooms.question: What changes when the subject stays the same but the source of the verdict changes?
rooms.ontology: A claim has a subject, a predicate, confidence and provenance. Four authored viewpoints attach different evaluations to the same subject identifier.
rooms.action: Read the subject ID on all four panels, then compare each verdict, confidence and footer. Keep the identical subject fixed in your comparison.
rooms.observable: SUBJECT #4729 is ORDERLY 87%, CREATIVE 64%, DANGEROUS 92% or IRRELEVANT 22%, depending on the panel. Each panel names its viewpoint.
rooms.mechanism: Four map placements explicitly set verdict NW, NE, SW and SE. A panel’s verdict is fixed from its configuration; walking changes which panel you read, not an input to a classifier.
rooms.limit: These percentages are authored signs, not calibrated probabilities. Different judgements can have unequal evidence; situatedness does not make every verdict equally credible.
rooms.variation: Existing: choose the highest confidence and ask what extra evidence would make it trustworthy. Proposed: reveal distinct measurement criteria and allow one same observation to be evaluated under each.
rooms.prior_bridge: The conflict sculpture kept two versions present; these panels retain the location of four judgements.
rooms.next_bridge: Collective knowledge asks how contributions can be combined without losing that provenance.

sources.fact: Four authored labels and confidences.

cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

rooms.question: When many marks accumulate, what makes the result knowledge rather than a pile?
rooms.ontology: A contribution is an event from a source; a shared artifact accumulates contributions. Participation counts and validation are different operations.
rooms.action: Follow a packet from a rim node to the central structure. Compare how the edit and contributor readouts change during the first growing structure.
rooms.observable: Packets from twelve peer positions add facets to a central helix. Repeated contributions can increase edits without introducing a new contributor.
rooms.mechanism: The script selects random peer indices and accepts each arriving packet, adding one authored facet. After sixty facets it clears the structure. It is a simulated accretion, not a live multi-user editor.
rooms.limit: The animation omits review, disagreement, exclusion and correction. The same rule accepting every contribution also accepts error; growing shape alone does not establish shared knowledge.
rooms.variation: Existing: count several contributions from an already seen peer. Proposed: tag a disputed contribution and make acceptance, revision and source history visible.
rooms.prior_bridge: Situated panels preserved competing sources; peer production attempts a common object.
rooms.next_bridge: The rhizome asks what connection pattern that common process builds.

rooms.question: Can a network grow through local connections without being given a root?
rooms.ontology: A graph has nodes and edges; this growth rule adds a spatial node and links it to nearby existing nodes. No root field or parent-child hierarchy is assigned.
rooms.action: Follow one new shoot and count its new links. Watch a locally crowded area and compare how often it receives a connection with a sparse area.
rooms.observable: Nodes and connecting segments accumulate while the NODES and EDGES readout changes. The structure restarts when its forty-node capacity is reached.
rooms.mechanism: Starting with two nodes, each timed shoot chooses a random position and connects to up to three nearest existing nodes. Geometric proximity and insertion time therefore shape degree.
rooms.limit: Having no designated root does not guarantee equal influence or resilience. Early or centrally located nodes can collect many links.
rooms.variation: Existing: identify a visually busy node and predict the effect of losing it. Proposed: remove it and compute components instead of assuming the network remains connected.
rooms.prior_bridge: Peer production accumulated contributions; the rhizome makes a connection rule visible.
rooms.next_bridge: The assembly laboratory next constrains which parts can connect and where they must go.

cautions: Source-reviewed draft; current museum reach, readable labels, controls and human learning unverified.

rooms.question: How can the same inventory become more than one recognisable body?
rooms.ontology: A catalogue names part types; an assembly assigns typed parts to target transforms and declares bonds. Motion towards targets is a separate mechanism from the chosen assembly.
rooms.action: Choose a recognisable part and follow it through floating and assembly phases. Wait for another assembly and compare which relations have changed.
rooms.observable: Forty pieces float, then move towards target positions; bond lines update between assigned parts. The scene cycles assemblies with ten-second float and assembly phases.
rooms.mechanism: The scene reads authored catalogues and assemblies from JSON. MolecularPart uses a damped spring towards a target and independent idle waves otherwise. These are authored assemblies, not a chemical search.
rooms.limit: A part name or bond line does not establish molecular chemistry. Predefined bodies can be recombined without making every possible body available.
rooms.variation: Existing: compare a named part’s role across two automatic arrangements. Proposed: author an assembly that the present catalogue makes awkward, then decide whether to change the inventory or its connection rules.
rooms.prior_bridge: Rhizome growth selected neighbours by proximity; here an explicit assembly defines targets and links.
rooms.next_bridge: The final ledger asks us to record what every such design choice makes difficult or impossible.

rooms.question: Can you name one person a useful design choice could leave out?
rooms.ontology: A decision has an intended benefit, an excluded case and an owner who can revisit it. Accountability needs a record and a subsequent response, not merely a confession.
rooms.action: Read one complete choice/exclusion pair before it scrolls away. State a specific change that would reduce that exclusion and one trade-off it would introduce.
rooms.observable: Example pairs such as a short name field and long names appear on the ledger; older lines leave the six-line display as new entries arrive.
rooms.mechanism: The artifact randomly displays ten prewritten pairs every1.8seconds. It does not capture visitor decisions, save a ledger or verify a repair.
rooms.limit: Naming exclusion cannot substitute for changing the condition that produces it. The prewritten groups are prompts, not evidence about a particular user.
rooms.variation: Existing discussion: return to one museum room and name one real rule, the encounter it prevents and a test for a proposed change. Proposed build: save that decision with its source, owner and next review.
rooms.prior_bridge: The assembly room made a catalogue’s permitted bodies visible; the ledger asks what those permissions leave outside.
rooms.next_bridge: Return to a chosen room, including Point One, with one concrete improvement and a way to observe its effect.
